summary: Iteration 6 fully verified. Backend pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_mfa_recovery.py = 8/8 PASSED covering: (1) POST /api/auth/mfa/recovery-request returns identical 200 anti-enumeration body for existing MFA-enabled user vs non-existent email; only existing MFA-enabled user gets a mfa_recoveries row inserted; (2) POST /api/auth/mfa/recovery-confirm returns 400 for garbage token; with an injected valid sha256 token it returns 200, sets mfa_enabled=false, unsets mfa_secret, bumps password_version and deletes user_sessions; second use of the same token returns 400 (single-use); (3) /api/auth/reset-password now PRESERVES mfa_enabled+mfa_secret when the user has no mfa_residual_test flag; (4) reset-password on a user WITH mfa_residual_test=true clears mfa (mfa_enabled=false, mfa_secret unset, mfa_residual_test unset); (5) regression: customer forgot -> injected reset token -> reset-password -> POST /auth/login returns 200 with token+user; (6) owner mgrodrigues920@gmail.com read-only snapshot matches after tests (untouched). Frontend: /recuperar-mfa (a) renders request form with mfa-recovery-email + mfa-recovery-request-btn; (b) submitting any email shows mfa-recovery-sent block with 'Se a conta existir e tiver MFA ativo…'; (c) with ?token=invalidgarbagexxx renders mfa-recovery-confirm and clicking mfa-recovery-confirm-btn triggers a sonner error toast 'Link inválido ou já utilizado'; (d) mfa-lost-link on LoginPage MFA screen — logged in with an injected MFA-enabled staff user (testmfaui...) whose backend correctly returned mfa_required=true; MFA screen shows the link text 'recupere o acesso por e-mail' with href=/recuperar-mfa; clicking navigates to the request form. All test users/sessions/mfa_recoveries/password_resets deleted. Owner state after tests: role=owner, mfa_enabled=true, mfa_residual_test=true (unchanged).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py forgot_password has a slightly ambiguous condition: `if user and user.get('password_hash') is not None or (user and payload.email.lower() == OWNER_EMAIL.lower())` — operator precedence means this evaluates as `(user and password_hash) or (user and email==owner)`, which is what's intended but wrapping the left clause in parens would make it explicit.

MfaRecoveryPage.jsx confirmRecovery uses toast.error with fallback text 'Link inválido ou expirado', while the backend actually returns 'Link inválido ou já utilizado' / 'Link expirado' / 'Link já utilizado'. In practice the backend detail is shown (verified via UI test), so the fallback text is only cosmetic — consider aligning the fallback to backend wording.

mfa_recoveries collection lacks a TTL index on expires_at; used tokens are marked used=true but never garbage-collected. Non-blocking, but a TTL index or a periodic sweep would keep the collection lean.
test_credentials: Ephemeral test users created in-run and deleted (prefixes testmfarec* and testmfaui*). Owner mgrodrigues920@gmail.com read-only.
seed_data_creation: In-test injections only: users testmfarec.*/testmfaui.*@example.com, mfa_recoveries rows, password_resets rows, user_sessions rows. All removed at end (mongosh count=0). Owner document untouched (snapshot vs post-run match).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full MFA recovery flow (request + confirm) works E2E; the LoginPage mfa-lost-link is only rendered while the MFA verification screen is active (state.mfa=true, mfa.setup=false). To force it in a UI test, inject an MFA-enabled user with a known argon2 password and log in via /login using auth-email/auth-password/auth-submit-btn — the backend replies mfa_required=true and LoginPage renders the MFA code screen with the link. Owner residual flag mfa_residual_test:true is still set on mgrodrigues920@gmail.com by the operator; only a real password-reset by the owner will consume it.
rca of the issue: N/A — iteration is a feature verification, no defects observed.
